findings.title: Shared context retains client certificates
findings.why_it_matters: After a request supplies a client certificate, urllib3 loads that certificate into the supplied SSLContext. Because every `verify=True` pool shares this module-level context, later verified requests to other hosts can present the earlier request's client certificate, even when those requests supplied no certificate. Give client-certificate requests an isolated context so the shared default context never retains per-request credentials.
findings.suggested_fix: Avoid using the shared default SSLContext for pools with client certificates; use a context isolated by client certificate (or an equivalent per-connection mechanism) while keeping the default CA bundle preloaded.
evidence: src/requests/adapters.py:102-105 -- client_cert paths are put into pool kwargs as cert_file and key_file; urllib3's ssl_wrap_socket loads a supplied cert_file/key_file into the provided SSLContext with load_cert_chain().
